QF.id: AIFM Fund Monitoring, Reporting, and Exit_7

question.text: Yamuna Opportunities Fund (close-ended Cat II) proposes a change of Investment Manager following acquisition of the sponsor. Under SEBI's master circular framework, dissenting unit-holders must be offered an exit. Which of the following statements is CORRECT regarding this process?

answer.text: No exit is required if the manager secures approval of 51% of unit-holders by value.
Exit is mandatory irrespective of consent thresholds; all investors may withdraw.
The exit requirement is waived if at least 75% of unit-holders by value of investment approve the change.
Dissenting investors must wait till fund maturity; SEBI does not provide interim exit rights.

explanation.text: The Logic: SEBI's material-change framework provides a mandatory exit window to dissenters UNLESS 75% of investors by value consent to the change. Dissenters get a 1-month dissent window and must be bought out within 3 months at a valuation averaged across two independent valuers, with costs borne by manager/sponsor (not the fund). The Trap: 51% is the ordinary-majority misconception. 'Mandatory irrespective' ignores the 75% carve-out. 'Wait till maturity' is false — material changes trigger statutory exit rights. Cross-Exam Context: III-A/C and XIX-A/B test this 75% threshold. XIX-C expects you to know the operational mechanics — valuer appointment, cost allocation, 3-month window. Manager's Pro-Tip: Before launching a 'control change' vote, pre-wire anchor LPs (typically 35-40% of NAV) and confirm the 75% path is achievable. If not, budget the dissent buy-out as a sponsor-level contingency — the manager cannot charge it to the fund.
